propositions.text: This is an appeal of a December 9, 2019 RPD decision denying refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: This is an appeal of a December 9, 2019 decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) of the Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (Board) denying the Appellant's claim for refugee protection under sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c. 27 (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The court states this is an appeal of the December 9, 2019 RPD decision denying refugee protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The Appellant, a Ukrainian national, joined the Party of Regions in 2002 and held a local position.
propositions.quote: The Appellant, a Ukrainian national, claims that, in 2002, he joined the Party of Regions and became the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in the village of XXXX.

propositions.text: After Yanukovych was ousted in 2014, Party members were persecuted and the Appellant was beaten and hospitalized for six days.
propositions.quote: After president Victor Yanukovych-the Party's candidate who had been elected president in 2010 -was ousted in the February 2014 revolution, members of the Party were persecuted and, on XXXX XXXX, 2014, the Appellant was beaten by two masked men, leading to his hospitalization for six days.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant says he joined the Party of Regions in 2002 and was beaten and hospitalized after Yanukovych's 2014 ouster.

propositions.text: In 2015, the Appellant was beaten after a Party meeting and hospitalized for 14 days.
propositions.quote: On XXXX XXXX, 2015, after meeting about the possible participation of the Party in the 2015 municipal election, the Appellant claims he was beaten by unknown assailants, leading to his hospitalization for 14 days.

propositions.text: In 2017, the Appellant was beaten again after preparing Party candidate registration documents and hospitalized for 16 days.
propositions.quote: Finally, on XXXX XXXX, 2017 (either in the afternoon or late at night1), the Appellant was beaten by unknown assailants and hospitalized for 16 days, after preparing the registration documents for a candidate from the Party.

propositions.text: After each attack, the Appellant contacted police but they could not assist.
propositions.quote: After each attack, he contacted the police, but they were unable to assist.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant says he was beaten in 2015 and 2017 after Party activities and police could not help.

propositions.text: After the 2017 attack, the Appellant applied for and received a Canadian visitor visa and flew to Toronto, leaving family behind.
propositions.quote: As a result of the XXXX 2017 attack, he applied for a Canadian visitor visa, which was issued on XXXX XXXX, 2017. On XXXX XXXX, 2017 he flew from Ukraine to Toronto, leaving behind his wife and two children.

propositions.text: He claims returning to Ukraine would expose him to persecution from the political bloc of former president Poroshenko.
propositions.quote: He claims that if he returns to Ukraine, he will face persecution from the "political bloc of Petr Poroshenko," president of Ukraine from June 2014 until April 2019.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant says he fled to Canada after 2017 attack fearing persecution from Poroshenko's political bloc if he returns.

propositions.text: The appeal is denied for reasons that follow.
propositions.quote: For the reasons that follow, I deny this appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The court denies the appeal for reasons explained later.

propositions.text: The Appellant included several news articles in the appeal record, some dated 2019 and others undated.
propositions.quote: The Appellant has included in his appeal record the several news article (or excepts therefrom), one of which is dated September 30, 2019; one of which is dated June 21, 2019; and the balance of which are undated.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submitted several news articles dated 2019 and undated as evidence in the appeal record.

propositions.text: Subsection 110(4) IRPA limits new evidence to that arising after RPD rejection, not reasonably available then, or not reasonably expected to be presented then.
propositions.quote: Subsection 110(4) of the IRPA limits the admission of evidence in an appeal before the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to evidence that: 1) arose after the RPD's rejection of the claim; 2) was not reasonably available at the time of the RPD's rejection of the claim; or 3) an appellant could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented at the time of the RPD's rejection of the claim.

propositions.text: Federal Court of Appeal in Singh and Raza cases elaborated factors for new evidence: newness, credibility, relevance, and modified materiality.
propositions.quote: The evidence must also meet the factors elaborated by the Federal Court of Appeal in the Singh case3 (where the Court relied on its earlier finding in the Raza case4), i.e. newness, credibility, relevance, and a modified version of materiality.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains subsection 110(4) IRPA and FCA cases require new evidence to meet strict criteria including newness and relevance.

propositions.text: RAD Rule 3(3)(g)(iii) requires full detailed submissions on how new evidence meets subsection 110(4) and relates to appellant.
propositions.quote: RAD Rule 3(3)(g)(iii)6 provides that an appellant seeking the admission of new evidence must provide full and detailed submissions regarding how the evidence meets the requirements of subsection 110(4) and how that evidence relates to the appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD Rule 3(3)(g)(iii) requires detailed submissions on new evidence admissibility and relevance to appellant.

propositions.text: The Appellant did not provide full detailed submissions on how documents comply with subsection 110(4).
propositions.quote: The full and detailed submissions required by RAD Rule 3(3)(g)(iii) have not been provided.

propositions.text: Appellant only referred to documents' relevance as proof of ongoing persecution and threats to Party followers in Ukraine.
propositions.quote: The Appellant's only reference to the documents pertains to their relevance: "We provided the Penal [sic] with the current violent country conditions in Ukraine confirming the ongoing persecution and threats to the followers of the Party of Region in the county. The new relevant proofs are enclosed to this Appeal."

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant failed to provide required detailed submissions; appellant only claimed documents show ongoing persecution.

propositions.text: Documents are inadmissible because appellant did not show compliance with subsection 110(4).
propositions.quote: Because the Appellant has not made submissions as to how the documents comply with subsection 110(4), I find that they are inadmissible.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the documents inadmissible due to lack of compliance submissions under subsection 110(4).

propositions.text: Even if lenient, the evidence does not meet subsection 110(4) as articles predate RPD rejection or are undated and were reasonably available then.
propositions.quote: I note that all of the articles are dated before the rejection of the claim by the RPD or are undated; as such they may not be said to have arisen after the rejection of the claim. Nor is there any indication that they were not reasonably available as of that date. I find that they do not meet the requirements of subsection 110(4) and, as such, are inadmissible.

paragraphs.summary: The court alternatively finds the evidence inadmissible as it predates RPD rejection and was reasonably available then.

propositions.text: Appellant's request for hearing on new evidence is denied as no new evidence admitted under subsection 110(6).
propositions.quote: Because no new evidence has been admitted, the request for a hearing pursuant to subsection 110(6) of the IRPA must be denied.

paragraphs.summary: The court denies appellant's hearing request because no new evidence was admitted.

propositions.text: The standard of review of the RPD decision is correctness as RPD had no meaningful advantage in findings.
propositions.quote: In my review of the RPD's decision, I will apply a standard of correctness. This is not a case where the RPD enjoyed a meaningful advantage in making its findings.

paragraphs.summary: The court states it will apply correctness standard to review the RPD decision.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellant's past persecution evidence speculative based on limited testimony about attackers' words and political link.
propositions.quote: The RPD held as follows: 1) The Appellant's evidence that he had been persecuted in the past due to his political activities was speculative. When asked if the attacks were political, he testified that he overheard one of his attackers saying: "Please do not stick your nose in things that you shouldn't stick his nose into." When asked by the RPD member if there was anything else about the assaults that caused him to think that they were related to his politics, he testified: "Yes, this was related to my membership in the party."

propositions.text: RPD found credibility problems: non-responsive answers, vagueness, contradictory employment history, lack of supporting Party evidence.
propositions.quote: 2) The Appellant had the following credibility problems: a) his answers were, at times, non-responsive; b) he was vague and evasive in his testimony, in particular in his attempt to explain that he had to hire someone to arrange for a visa for him (based on false information) because the Ukrainian government was preventing the Canadian government from issuing visas to Party of Regions supporters; c) his claimed employment history was contradictory (in his port of entry notes he said he worked for the XXXX of former president Yanukovych, in his testimony he said that before coming to Canada he worked in XXXX with his son and for XXXX, and in his Schedule A form he said that he held a XXXX position working as a "XXXX XXXX" for former president Yanukovych from XXXX 2013 to XXXX 2014); and d) he lacked evidence from Party officials showing he was a member and that he had been attacked, which should have been reasonably available.

propositions.text: RPD found supporting evidence deficient: wife's health not linked to persecution, doctor's note unsupported, letters unverified.
propositions.quote: 3) His supporting evidence was deficient: a) his claim that his wife's health problems were linked to his treatment in Ukraine was not supported by the medical reports or by common sense (rheumatoid arthritis is not caused by being married to someone who has been persecuted); b) a doctor's note stating that he has experienced depression and anxiety warranted no weight because it does not support his claim about what happened in Ukraine and it is not clear what it is based on; and c) two handwritten letters from people who allege that they are friends of his and Party members deserve no weight because there were no identity documents accompanying them and the RPD had no independent verification of the authors' identity.

propositions.text: RPD found no evidence that ordinary Party members continue to be individually targeted years after 2014 uprising.
propositions.quote: 4) As to a general profile, while there is country condition evidence that there was violence among Party supporters in connection with the popular uprising in 2014, there was no evidence to support his claim that ordinary Party members continue to be individually targeted years afterwards.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found appellant's persecution evidence speculative, credibility issues, deficient supporting evidence, and no ongoing targeting of Party members.

propositions.text: Appellant argues he could not get Party evidence because Party dispersed and documents destroyed after 2014 overthrow.
propositions.quote: In reply to the RPD's finding at 2(d), he argues that he could not get supporting evidence from the Party because after the 2014 overthrow, the Party was dispersed and the documentation was destroyed: "political and information censorship swept over Ukraine and there are no possibilities to obtain the updated documents."

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred in finding no past persecution or political profile supporting future targeting claim.
propositions.quote: In reply to the RPD's finding 4, he argues that it erred in stating that the Appellant had not established he was persecuted in the past or has a political profile that would support his allegation that he would be targeted in the future based upon his past.

propositions.text: Appellant argues civil resistance and persecution of Party members increased after 2014 overthrow, shown by country and new evidence.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that since the 2014 overthrow, civil resistance and disobedience in Ukraine has grown, resulting in new street fights and persecution of Party members. He states that this is shown by the country condition evidence provided to the RPD and the new evidence submitted with this appeal.

propositions.text: Appellant argues he was not unresponsive or evasive but had psychological conditions affecting communication, supported by doctor's certificate.
propositions.quote: In response to the RPD's findings at 2(a) and (b), he argues that he was not unresponsive, vague, or evasive. Rather, he had psychological conditions and took medications that caused difficulties in his communication skills-as shown by a certificate from his family doctor.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred on employment inconsistencies due to translation error; political activity was voluntary.
propositions.quote: In response to the RPD's finding at 2(c), he argues that the RPD erred in finding inconsistencies about where he worked. There was an interpretation error because "work" in the Ukrainian language means only "permanent employment, making money." His political activity as a member of the Party was on a voluntary basis.

propositions.text: Appellant argues medical certificates confirm health conditions started after persecution and relate to serious concerns for family.
propositions.quote: In response to the RPD's finding at 3(a) and (b), he argues that the medical certificates he provided to the RPD "confirm [that] the medical conditions of his wife and himself have started after the threats and persecutions of 2014-2016 and the diagnosis of hypertension, depression, and anxiety are directly related to the serious concerns of the life and health of the claimants and his family members."

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues errors in RPD findings on evidence availability, persecution, communication, employment, and medical conditions.

propositions.text: Party did not cease to exist after 2014; attacks in 2015 and 2017 related to Party candidate support.
propositions.quote: While it is clear from the evidence that the Party of Regions suffered serious losses in 2014, there is no evidence that it ceased to exist at that time. Indeed, according to the Appellant's own evidence, the attacks against him in 2015 and 2017 were both related to his efforts in support of Party candidates.

propositions.text: No evidence of destroyed Party documents or lack of archives; memorandum is not evidence.
propositions.quote: Nor is there any evidence regarding the destruction of Party documents or the lack of archives. (Clearly the memorandum is not a means by which the Appellant's counsel may introduce evidence of her view of the state of affairs in Ukraine.)

propositions.text: Appellant made no attempt to obtain evidence from former Party officials, only from former members.
propositions.quote: I note further that the evidence does not show that the Appellant made any attempt to obtain evidence from former Party officials-something he did do with former Party members.

propositions.text: New evidence requested is inadmissible; country evidence does not support claim of future targeting of Party members at appellant's level.
propositions.quote: As noted above, the new evidence which the Appellant requested the admission of has been found inadmissible. Based on my review of the country condition evidence as contained in the National Documentation Package (NDP), as well as the extracts of news articles provided by the Appellant to the RPD, I agree with the RPD that the objective evidence does not support his claim that a party member at his level would be targeted into the future.

propositions.text: A 2019 Ontario clinic letter notes appellant's anxiety and depression but lacks link to testimony issues and medical expertise on risk to Ukraine.
propositions.quote: A XXXX XXXX XXXX 2019 letter from a walk-in clinic in XXXX, Ontario states that the Appellant "complains about anxiety and depression with migraine headache and panic attack [sic]" and notes that he has been prescribed anti-depressants. In addition, the doctor states "I advised him of not returning [sic] to Ukraine as that will endanger his life." First, I note that no link between the Appellant's conditions and his ability to testify coherently and directly is made in the letter. Moreover, I note that the doctor's statement about the risk to the Appellant in Ukraine-a statement made without any supporting reasoning and outside his area of expertise-undermines the overall value of the letter.

propositions.text: The letter shows the doctor acted as advocate, undermining its value; no evidence appellant's mental health caused evasive testimony.
propositions.quote: It shows that the letter's author, instead of providing evidence as a neutral expert, has become an advocate of the Appellant, or at the very least shown a willingness to provide non-medical opinions in a medical letter. Without evidence that the Appellant had a medical condition that would result in testimony that was unresponsive, vague, or evasive, I am unable to find that his mental health provides a justification for the nature of his testimony.

propositions.text: No indication appellant has mental condition affecting testimony beyond counsel's statements; court agrees with RPD's assessment of testimony quality.
propositions.quote: Again, it is not appropriate for the Appellant's counsel to offer evidence. I agree with the RPD's assessment of the quality of his testimony.

propositions.text: Counsel's memorandum is not evidence; translation argument rejected for lack of evidence.
propositions.quote: Once again, the Appellant's counsel appears to believe that a legal memorandum represents an opportunity for her to provide evidence-this time about the proper translation of certain words from Ukrainian into English. I am unable to accept arguments about the quality of the translation in the absence of evidence

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Party still exists, no evidence of destroyed documents, inadmissible new evidence, no medical link to testimony issues, and rejects counsel's evidence.

propositions.text: Considering credibility problems and lack of evidence, no serious possibility of persecution or harm upon return to Ukraine.
propositions.quote: I have considered the Appellant's credibility problems-including the lack of reasonably available documentation without reasonable explanation; the evasive and non-responsive nature of his testimony, in particular about the interference of the Ukrainian state with the ability of members of the Party to obtain Canadian visas; and the inconsistency in the Appellant's evidence about when he worked as an XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX-and the dearth of evidence showing that he had been subjected to persecution based on his political views or that he was likely to be persecuted in the future. When I weigh this against the supporting evidence that does exist, I find that there is not a serious possibility that he will face persecution or a likelihood of other harm upon his return to Ukraine.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds appellant's credibility issues and lack of evidence mean no serious risk of persecution or harm if returned to Ukraine.

propositions.text: The Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a protected person; appeal dismissed.
propositions.quote: The Appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a protected person. The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes appellant is not a refugee or protected person and dismisses the appeal.
